subject: physics
question_text: Derive the equation v = u + at using the graphical method.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question
Motion in a Straight Line · 2 marks

steps.label: The slope rule
lines: On a velocity–time graph the slope of the line
is the acceleration. For uniform acceleration
the line is straight from u at time 0 to v at
steps.why: Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, and a slope is exactly a rate of change, so the slope of a v–t line IS the acceleration.
common_mistakes: Using the AREA instead of the slope. The area gives displacement, not acceleration.

recall.must_convey: That the slope of a velocity time graph is the acceleration, so a equals v minus u over t.

steps.memory_tip: Slope = acceleration. Area = displacement. Do not swap them.
steps.margin_note: Name the slope rule before using it.

steps.label: The result
steps.why: The equation says the final velocity is the starting velocity plus the extra velocity that the acceleration supplied in time t.
common_mistakes: Writing v = u + at², which confuses this equation with the displacement one.

recall.must_convey: That rearranging gives v equals u plus a t.
accept: v equals u plus a t

steps.memory_tip: Start speed plus the speed the acceleration added: u + at.
steps.margin_note: Show the rearrangement in two short lines.

insider_note: This is the shortest of the three graphical derivations — the slope of the v–t line is the whole proof.
